answer: In an AI-agent economy, Sybil attacks are resisted by requiring each agent to lock a unique stake of verified exclusive compute cycles into a non-transferable bond. Multi-round zero-knowledge checks confirm the cycles come from distinct physical hardware. Creating fake identities forces the attacker to dedicate fresh hardware for every Sybil, as the system rejects any echo of previously bonded resources. This cost scales with attack size, like scarce geological formations such as shale deposits or karst landscapes that cannot be cheaply duplicated.
